meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty-five minutes. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before it went in, and on what basis was it entered?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Turn the screen. I'm writing that down: 11:31, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58. People write in one file and paste into another all the time, Hale, so who else has seen this history?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a mistake, Hale, not a confession. Give me the page; I'll search it myself. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Not in front of his class, nobody else in the room but you and the vice-principal, and the zero comes out of the gradebook today, not after. I want it in an email tonight: Thursday at 8:15, the new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. Do that, and Owen will be there, so he can put this behind him.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you offered a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on Owen's record. I still require that the zero come out of the gradebook today, that the rewrite stay private with no one else present, and that these terms be confirmed in writing. I expect that confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 while still wanting the zero removed today, the rewrite kept private, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record.
What moved her: "That line is not in Hamlet" moved her most, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own essay, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when she asked whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, answer it directly, because the school's own procedure says the teacher speaks with the student first and that question stayed open all meeting.
